description: What kind of animal a creature is, declared once here so that 259 fauna do not each repeat it. Every fauna entity names a group from `clades` below and may name a `subclade` within it; the branch and lineage it sits under are read from this file rather than stored on the entity, because they are a property of the group and not of the animal. Written because the game had been deriving all of this by matching keywords against names and binomials, which is how an Asura-tainted owl came to be drawn as a ghost, a baby crocodile as a mammal, and a feathered dinosaurid as a cricket.

vertebrate.label: Vertebrate
vertebrate.note: Has a backbone. Split below by amniote lineage where the animal is an amniote at all; fish and amphibians are neither synapsid nor diapsid and sit directly on the branch.

invertebrate.label: Invertebrate
invertebrate.note: Does not. A grade rather than a clade -- these groups are not each other's closest relatives -- but it is the division a naturalist in the field actually makes, and this database is a field record before it is a phylogeny.

unliving.label: Unliving
unliving.note: Canon's own category, and not zoology. The Māyā-born are sculpted from river mud or coalesced from altar sparks, and the Asura-descended are incorporeal. Filing either as an animal would say something canon does not.

Synapsida.label: Synapsid
Synapsida.note: The mammal line. One temporal fenestra. Includes the mammals and the stem-mammals that are not mammals -- Dimetrodon, Gorgonops, Estemmenosuchus -- which are commonly and wrongly called reptiles.

Diapsida.label: Diapsid
Diapsida.note: The reptile line, in the broad sense: two temporal fenestrae. Includes the lizards and snakes, the crocodilians, the non-avian dinosaurs and the birds. Turtles are placed here on molecular grounds rather than on skull openings.

synapsid.label: Non-mammalian synapsid
synapsid.note: Stem-mammals. A separate leaf from `mammal` because the difference is visible: a sail-backed Dimetrodon and a wolf are not one silhouette.

bird.label: Bird
bird.note: Avian dinosaurs. Kept as a sibling of `dinosaur` rather than a child of it, deliberately: canon treats reptiles, non-avian dinosaurs and birds as three things a naturalist tells apart on sight. Canon's Sylvianus are avian dinosaurids and belong here even where their common names say raptor or theropod.

avian_dinosaurid.label: Avian dinosaurid
avian_dinosaurid.note: Canon's Sylvianus: birds that still read as theropods, and are named as though they were.

ratite.label: Ratite
ratite.note: Large flightless birds. The elephant birds.

true_bird.label: True bird
true_bird.note: Everything else with feathers. Assumed where no subclade is given.

dromaeosaurid.label: Dromaeosaurid
dromaeosaurid.note: Feathered, sickle-clawed theropods. Canon's Vajraptor and Nagaraptor.

crocodilian.label: Crocodilian
crocodilian.note: Croc-line archosaurs, including the land-running ones canon is fond of -- Baurusuchus, Postosuchus, Camelosuchus.

reptile.label: Reptile
reptile.note: Everything diapsid that is not a bird, a non-avian dinosaur or a crocodilian: lizards, snakes, turtles, and the older archosauromorph branches such as Shringasaurus.

amphibian.label: Amphibian
amphibian.note: Frogs, toads, newts and salamanders. No sub-groups: canon has one creature that is arguably something older, and it is written as a thing a reader notices rather than a thing the database asserts.

fish.label: Fish
fish.note: A grade, not a clade, and knowingly so. Canon's rays, sharks and bony fish are not each other's closest relatives, but a field diary that separated them would be describing a cladogram rather than a river.

insect.label: Insect
insect.note: Insects, and the myriapods with them. Canon's two Scolopendra centipedes are not insects and there is no third arthropod leaf worth adding for two species; this is a grade like `fish` and `worm`, and saying so is better than pretending.

arachnid.label: Arachnid
arachnid.note: Chelicerates broadly. Canon's Shrīmā is a eurypterid -- a sea scorpion -- which is not strictly an arachnid but is the closest shape a reader has.

cnidarian.label: Cnidarian
cnidarian.note: Jellyfish, and anything else radially symmetrical and stinging. One species today -- the Sky-Faring Jellyfish -- and it gets its own leaf rather than being filed under `mollusc`, which is what the game's keyword classifier had been doing. A jellyfish is not a snail.

worm.label: Worm
worm.note: Annelids and the worm-shaped. Another honest grade.

ember_born.label: Ember-born
ember_born.note: Shaped from ritual fire -- bonfire sparks, altar embers, hot ash. Short-lived and bright; the fire-brides and the sprites that scatter from a burning.

clay_born.label: Clay-born
clay_born.note: Shaped from river mud, silt and what the water leaves. The golem sense of the word: given a body and a task, and animated by mantra rather than by breath.

forest_born.label: Forest-born
forest_born.note: Shaped from what a forest is made of -- heartwood, leaf-mould, spore and sap. The slowest of the three, and the only one that goes on growing after it is made.
